pool.text: Bordeaux Cathedral was consecrated by Pope Urban II and dedicated to Saint Andrew.
The city cathedral St-André was built, incorporating the artisan quarter of Saint-Paul.
Pope Eugene IV created a university in the town by demand of Pey Berland.
The city of Bordeaux created a local parliament during its historical governance developments.
The army of Louis XIV entered Bordeaux as it was annexed to France.
Traders and merchants in Bordeaux began turning their attention toward the slave trade.
The National Convention abolished the university during the course of the French Revolution.
Napoleon revoked the manumission law but ultimately lost the war against former slaves.
Since the Liberation, there have been seven mayors serving the city of Bordeaux.
The metropolis received the Europe Prize for its efforts transmitting the European ideal.
The European Short Film Festival of Bordeaux has been held in the city.
The Bordeaux International Festival of Women in Cinema took place in the city.
The Port of the Moon in historic Bordeaux was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
The Bordeaux International Independent Film Festival was established to showcase independent cinema.
Europe's longest and tallest vertical-lift bridge opened, spanning the River Garonne.
The city known as the Pearl of Aquitaine was voted European Destination of the year.
The Cité du Vin museum opened its doors with exhibitions and seminars on wine.
The LGV Sud Europe Atlantique became fully operational, shortening journey times to Paris.
A statue of Modeste Testas, an enslaved Ethiopian woman, was unveiled in the city.
Bordeaux was shortlisted for the European Commission's European Capital of Smart Tourism award.
